title: Residency enforcement metrics & events (draft)
body:
Context
- Project: Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning + deterministic enforcement + clear errors)
- This doc is an observability draft: proposed metrics/events, naming conventions, and example queries for:
  (1) detecting cross-region attempts (routing/fallback)
  (2) measuring block-rate by customer/org/project
  (3) tracking policy-evaluation latency + failure modes

Assumptions / definitions (aligning with ADR-021 boundaries)
- “Customer content” must not move outside allowed regions. Observability MUST avoid emitting customer content cross-region.
- “Residency decision” happens at request time (gateway + routing). We want end-to-end attribution:
  - what policy applied
  - what region was requested/selected
  - whether a cross-region fallback was attempted
  - whether request was blocked
- Dedicated: same metric names apply where components are shared; add deployment_mode label.

Metric design goals
- High signal, low cardinality by default.
- Ability to slice by org/project/customer for troubleshooting, BUT only via logs/traces (or sampled metrics) to avoid metric label explosion.
- A single source of truth for ‘blocked due to residency’ that matches the public error contract.
- Separate “attempted cross-region routing” vs “blocked by policy” vs “misconfiguration / no eligible region.”

Naming conventions
- Prefix: redwood.residency.* for enforcement-related metrics.
- Use dot-separated namespaces, with consistent suffixes:
  - *.requests_total (counter)
  - *.blocked_total (counter)
  - *.attempts_total (counter)
  - *.latency_ms (histogram)
  - *.errors_total (counter)
- Labels (keep minimal; prefer enums):
  - deployment_mode: hosted|dedicated|private (private may be N/A for this phase, but keep the label consistent)
  - component: gateway|routing|policy_service
  - endpoint: chat_completions|completions|embeddings|rerank|other (coarse bucket)
  - region: internal region id for where the request would execute (e.g., eu-west-1, us-east-1) — for selected_region metric only
  - requested_region: if present in request (most won’t set it; pinning is server-side)
  - policy_scope: org|project|api_key|none
  - policy_mode: enforce|monitor|disabled (if we have a flag-based monitor-only mode)
  - decision: allow|block
  - block_reason: enum only (see below)
  - error_code: enum only (matches ADR-022 codes)

Block reasons (enum set - draft)
- no_policy (should map to allow; only used for decision context)
- selected_region_not_allowed
- cross_region_fallback_disallowed
- no_eligible_region (allowed set empty / no healthy capacity in allowed regions)
- invalid_policy_config (control plane bug / should page)
- policy_evaluation_error (policy service timeout/error)
- routing_decision_error (unexpected internal error)

Public error codes (enum - align with ADR-022)
- RESIDENCY_POLICY_VIOLATION
- RESIDENCY_NO_ELIGIBLE_REGION
- RESIDENCY_POLICY_EVALUATION_FAILED
(Note: finalize exact strings with Brian/Amara; metrics should mirror the final list.)

Core metrics (P0)
1) Request classification + decision outcomes
- redwood.residency.enforcement.requests_total
  - counter incremented for requests that pass through enforcement code-path
  - labels: deployment_mode, component, endpoint, policy_mode
- redwood.residency.enforcement.decisions_total
  - counter incremented once per request (at gateway, authoritative)
  - labels: deployment_mode, endpoint, policy_scope, policy_mode, decision, block_reason, error_code
  - NOTE: avoid org_id in labels.

2) Cross-region routing attempts
- redwood.residency.routing.cross_region_attempts_total
  - counter incremented whenever routing would pick a region not in allowed set (including fallback)
  - labels: deployment_mode, endpoint, policy_scope, policy_mode, attempt_type
  - attempt_type: primary_not_allowed|fallback_not_allowed|capacity_spillover|other
- redwood.residency.routing.selected_region_total
  - counter: region selected for execution (only when allowed)
  - labels: deployment_mode, endpoint, region, policy_scope, policy_mode

3) Policy evaluation latency + errors
- redwood.residency.policy.eval_latency_ms
  - histogram
  - labels: deployment_mode, policy_scope, policy_mode
- redwood.residency.policy.eval_errors_total
  - counter
  - labels: deployment_mode, policy_scope, policy_mode, error_type
  - error_type: timeout|5xx|invalid_response|cache_miss_burst|other

4) Gateway response classification
- redwood.api.errors_total (existing) should include:
  - labels include error_code=RESIDENCY_* when policy blocks
  - ensure streaming + non-streaming share the same error_code values
- Add specific convenience counter if needed:
  - redwood.residency.gateway.blocks_total
    - labels: deployment_mode, endpoint, error_code, block_reason

5) End-to-end SLO guardrails (supporting false-positive detection)
- redwood.residency.enforcement.block_rate
  - derived: decisions_total{decision="block"} / decisions_total
  - dashboards should show:
    - global
    - by endpoint
    - by region (selected region) where possible

Logs & traces: structured events (P0)
Goal: enable per-customer/org diagnostics without high-cardinality metric labels.

Add/standardize these fields on gateway request logs and trace spans (no prompt/content):
- request_id (existing)
- org_id (string, in logs only; NOT in metric labels)
- project_id (string, logs only)
- api_key_id (string, logs only; consider hashing; confirm with Security)
- residency_policy_id (string; exposure in logs ok; public response TBD)
- policy_scope (org|project|api_key|none)
- policy_mode (enforce|monitor|disabled)
- allowed_regions (array -> log as comma-separated string; careful with size; typically small)
- primary_region
- requested_region (if present)
- selected_region (routing outcome)
- cross_region_attempted (bool)
- cross_region_reason (enum)
- decision (allow|block)
- block_reason (enum)
- error_code (RESIDENCY_*)
- http_status
- enforcement_component_version (git sha or build)

Event emission (audit + product analytics style)
- Audit log events (separate from metrics, but mention for completeness):
  - residency_policy.created / updated / deleted
  - residency_policy.override_enabled (if we implement emergency bypass)
- Runtime “enforcement block event” (internal event stream) (optional P1):
  - residency_enforcement.blocked_request
  - intended for: support tooling + console “blocked requests” view
  - payload should be content-free; use request_id and decision context only

Dashboards (draft layout)
A) Overview: ‘Residency enforcement health’
- Total requests through enforcement
- Block rate (global)
- Block reasons stacked area
- Policy eval latency p50/p95/p99
- Policy eval error rate

B) Cross-region attempts
- cross_region_attempts_total over time
- Top attempt_type
- Selected region breakdown (allowed traffic) to spot hotspots

C) Endpoint parity (streaming vs non-streaming)
- Blocks + error_code distribution per endpoint
- Specifically watch streaming endpoints returning generic 5xx instead of RESIDENCY_* (regression from SUP-28577)

D) Customer troubleshooting (links only; powered by logs)
- Saved log queries by org_id/project_id
- Quick links from request_id -> trace -> gateway log -> routing decision log

Alerting (draft thresholds; needs SRE tuning)
- Page (sev2): sudden spike in blocks due to policy_evaluation_error
  - condition: redwood.residency.policy.eval_errors_total rate > baseline*X for 5m
- Page (sev2): blocks_total increases > N% globally after deploy (false-positive risk)
- Ticket (sev3): cross_region_attempts_total increases (could indicate capacity pressure causing spillover attempts)
- Ticket (sev3): policy eval p99 > 100ms for 10m (tune)

Sample queries
(Examples shown in PromQL-ish style; adapt to Datadog/Chronosphere as needed.)

1) Global block rate
- sum(rate(redwood_residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="block"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_residency_enforcement_decisions_total[5m]))

2) Block rate by endpoint
- sum by (endpoint) (rate(redwood_residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="block"}[5m]))
  /
  sum by (endpoint) (rate(redwood_residency_enforcement_decisions_total[5m]))

3) Top block reasons (last 1h)
- topk(10, sum by (block_reason) (increase(redwood_residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="block"}[1h])))

4) Cross-region attempts vs blocks
- sum(rate(redwood_residency_routing_cross_region_attempts_total[5m]))
- sum(rate(redwood_residency_gateway_blocks_total[5m]))

5) Policy evaluation latency p95
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_residency_policy_eval_latency_ms_bucket[5m])))

6) Identify possible misconfig / empty allowed set
- sum(rate(redwood_residency_enforcement_decisions_total{block_reason="no_eligible_region"}[5m]))

Log query examples (pseudo)
- Find blocked requests for a specific org in last 15m:
  - service=gateway AND decision=block AND org_id="org_..." AND error_code startswith "RESIDENCY_" | fields timestamp, request_id, project_id, endpoint, block_reason, selected_region, allowed_regions

- Find cross-region attempts that did NOT end in block (should be near zero in enforce mode):
  - component=routing AND cross_region_attempted=true AND decision=allow AND policy_mode=enforce

Cardinality notes / explicit do-nots
- DO NOT add org_id/project_id/api_key_id as metric labels.
- allowed_regions should not be a label (explodes). Keep it in logs only.
- region label only on selected_region_total (bounded set), not on decisions_total.

Open questions / TODO
- Finalize canonical error_code strings with ADR-022 owners (Brian/Amara). Metrics must match SDK mapping.
- Do we have monitor-only mode? If yes, ensure metrics differentiate monitor blocks vs enforce blocks (policy_mode label).
- Are we allowed to log residency_policy_id broadly? Need Security sign-off (Marcus) on exposure + retention.
- Confirm where the authoritative decision metric lives (gateway vs routing). Current proposal: gateway emits decisions_total; routing emits attempts/selection.
- Decide whether to sample a per-org block rate metric (e.g., top-N heavy orgs) for quicker detection without full log scans.

Next steps (for ENG-4846)
- Align metric names with existing Redwood conventions (check redwood.api.* / redwood.routing.* patterns).
- Add counters/histograms to gateway + routing services.
- Add saved queries + dashboard panels (see Confluence monitoring spec).
- Validate streaming path emits consistent error_code + status and increments decisions_total exactly once.
